target_name: Independence From Both Markets and Lenders
rationale: Economically coherent and internally consistent, but it is essentially a mechanical average of two already-archived legs (hidden-knowledge-capital × net buyback, and researcher × Δnon-financial claim share) bolted onto the same intangible conditioner, so any improvement in fmb/alpha would be a portfolio-blending artifact rather than new economic information.

This is a genuine ablation of the archive's best negative signal — swapping the gross-profit leg (an inverse-profitability confound) for a claim-structure shift — and the expression's direction matches the stated negative hypothesis, so it is diagnostic regardless of outcome.

Averaging the level and the one-year change of the identical ratio, both of which were already tested separately with near-identical alphas, is a cosmetic smoothing variant that cannot distinguish between the two mechanisms it claims to unify.

target_name: Distribution Rate Out of Internally Generated Cash
rationale: The coverage diagnosis is sound, but this is the fifth denominator variant of the same buyback × hidden-R&D-capital family, and the ratio is sign-unstable when gross profit is near zero or negative (a negative numerator over a negative denominator ranks as strongly positive), which winsorizing at 1% does not fix.

Industry-demeaning the non-financial claim share directly targets the most obvious confound in a newly discovered channel (business-model-driven payables/deferred-revenue levels), and the construction cleanly matches the stated within-industry hypothesis.

The dominant leg is NEG(gross profit/at), a straight inversion of the published gross-profitability anomaly that the proposer concedes has driven the slope in every prior negative signal, so the claimed attribution of incremental content to claim composition is not identified by this construction.
